value.name: Cervical Spondylosis
value.description: Cervical spondylosis is a general term for age-related wear and tear affecting the spinal disks in your neck. As the disks dehydrate and shrink, signs of bone-on-bone contact appear. It is the most common cause of neck pain.
symptoms: Headaches, often starting in the back of the head
Grinding or popping sensation when moving the neck
Limited range of motion in the neck
Numbness or weakness in arms, hands, or legs

value.name: Herniated Cervical Disk
value.description: A herniated cervical disk occurs when the soft inner material of a spinal disk in the neck pushes out through a tear in the tougher exterior. This can put pressure on the spinal cord or nerves, leading to pain and other symptoms.
symptoms: Neck pain that may radiate to the shoulder and arm
Numbness or tingling in the arm or hand
Muscle weakness in the arm or hand
Pain that worsens with certain movements

value.name: Neck Strain
value.description: A neck strain, often called a 'stiff neck,' is an injury to the muscles or tendons in the neck. It typically results from overstretching or tearing of these tissues, often due to sudden movements or poor posture.

value.name: Meningitis
value.description: Meningitis is an inflammation of the membranes (meninges) surrounding the brain and spinal cord. It can be caused by viral, bacterial, or fungal infections, and can be a serious condition requiring prompt medical attention.

value.name: Fibromyalgia
value.description: Fibromyalgia is a disorder characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain accompanied by fatigue, sleep, memory, and mood issues. While it affects the whole body, neck pain is a very common symptom reported by individuals with this condition.
symptoms: Stiffness, particularly in the neck and shoulders
